issue: The '1 · FACT' node lists 'request rate ~2 rps / utilization 45% / baseline TTFT p99 450 ms' as if they were gathered FACTs, but the prose of the same capstone (PDF 410 / printed 390, Step 1) explicitly states these are 'assumed baseline inputs, not gathered FACTs (R-07): no author-run load test produced them ... not a measured runtime quantity a FACT would be.' The figure therefore mis-scopes assumed inputs as measured evidence, violating the book's own evidence-label discipline (R-07 / Ch. 4 axis taxonomy).
evidence: Fig 26.2 box 1 header reads '1 · FACT' with body 'request rate ~2 rps / utilization 45% / baseline TTFT p99 450 ms'. Page 410: 'These are assumed baseline inputs, not gathered FACTs (R-07) ... They become FACTs only once instrumented and recorded in a genuine load test.' The 450 ms is the assumed service-time sum 320+80+50, described on 410 as 'a scenario input, not a derived quantile of a distributed sample.'
acceptance_test: Relabel the node so it does not present the assumed 2 rps / 45% / 450 ms as gathered FACTs — e.g. split it into a 'READ: workload fingerprint' FACT node (short prompt, latency-sensitive, moderate quality) plus an 'ASSUMED BASELINE' node for the 2 rps / 45% / 450 ms, or rename the box 'INPUTS (assumed baseline)'. After the change, a reader comparing the figure to page 410 must find no statement that the 450 ms or 2 rps is a measured FACT.

issue: The DERIVED node states 'decode bandwidth-bound' as a clean conclusion, but the prose (page 410, Step 2) hedges it: 'batch size, context precision, kernel, and hardware decide whether it stays there.' The figure drops the conditionality, risking the exact 'decode is always bandwidth-bound' misconception the book warns against.
evidence: Fig 26.2 box 2 body: 'decode bandwidth-bound' (no qualifier). Page 410: '...so decode lands in the bandwidth-bound regime (the low-batch regime of Ch. 8; batch size, context precision, kernel, and hardware decide whether it stays there).'
acceptance_test: Add a short qualifier to the DERIVED node (e.g. 'decode bandwidth-bound (low-batch regime)') or a footnote marker tying it to the page-410 conditionality, so the figure no longer reads as an unconditional law.

evidence: Rendered page 413 shows the title, subtitle, and a compact 3-box loop in the top half, with a large empty region below the caption.
acceptance_test: Enlarge the diagram (boxes, arrows, and labels) so it is vertically centered and fills a greater share of the page, or move the caption/subtitle to balance the whitespace; confirm no label is clipped at the new size.

issue: The core distinction the figure encodes — 'blue = where the system runs' vs 'green = where the model runs' (the basis of the callout 'Model intelligence ≠ system intelligence') — is carried by hue only. In grayscale the two palettes overlap: the medium-blue band 'Inside agent runtime' and the medium-green band 'Inside attention' render at similar mid-grays, and the light-blue 'Inside tools' / light-green 'Inside weights' likewise. A print reader cannot map the legend's color words to the bands, so the system-vs-model split (the figure's main message) is lost. No non-color cue (border style, hatching, divider, or bracket) separates the two groups.
evidence: Legend line: 'blue = where the system runs · green = where the model runs'. Bands 2–5 use a blue gradient, bands 6–8 a green gradient; all share the same solid-border style, so hue is the only group discriminator. The red left arrow and red callout box remain visible in grayscale, but they do not encode the blue/green split.
acceptance_test: Add a non-color cue separating the system group (top 5 bands) from the model group (bottom 3 bands) — e.g. a horizontal divider line with a small 'SYSTEM' / 'MODEL' bracket label on the left, or distinct border styles/hatching per group — and re-verify in a grayscale render that a reader can identify which bands are 'system' vs 'model' without using the color words in the legend.

figure: Figure A.4 (Shared weights do not remove executed work), 'Actual stop' row
issue: In the 'Actual stop' row the solid flow line from 'pass 2' appears to enter the dashed 'pass 3 (not executed)' box and then continue to 'exit', visually placing the not-executed step on the execution path. This contradicts the 'not executed' label, the legend ('dashed box = not executed'), and the figure's purpose (an early exit removes pass 3's work). A reader can plausibly infer that pass 3 runs, which is the opposite of the intended contrast with the 'Post-hoc selection' row (where all three passes run).
evidence: Rendered 'Actual stop' row: pass 1 → pass 2, then a solid line/arrow into the dashed 'pass 3' box (captioned 'not executed'), then a solid arrow to the tan 'exit' box. Compare 'Post-hoc selection' row where pass 3 is a solid (executed) box. Legend: 'Solid arrows = flow; dashed box = not executed.'
acceptance_test: Redraw the 'Actual stop' row so the solid flow arrow goes directly from 'pass 2' to 'exit'; the dashed 'pass 3' box must carry no incoming flow arrow (show it as a skipped/omitted element, e.g. a bypass line over it or a 'skipped' tag). At print size a reader must not be able to infer that pass 3 executes on the actual-stop path.

issue: The subtitle 'vs each model's own predecessor' is not accurate for the GLM-5.3-Flash row, whose stated baseline is GLM-5.3 (the same-generation base model, not a predecessor). The caption correctly generalizes this to 'each model's own stated reference,' so the subtitle over-specifies and is locally inconsistent with the GLM row.
evidence: Subtitle: 'vs each model's own predecessor'. GLM row 'own baseline' column: 'vs GLM-5.3'. Caption: '...each model's vendor-reported ratio of its own stated reference (e.g. DeepSeek V4 vs V3.2)...'
acceptance_test: Change the subtitle to match the caption's wording, e.g. 'vs each model's own stated reference (predecessor or base model)', so the GLM-5.3 baseline is not mislabeled a predecessor.
